rulings.challenge_claim: The refrain warrant and the closing mark check out exactly, but a byte-true flight-from-terror device that begins inside this span at 2:10 recurs past the row's closing seam at 2:19 and 2:21 and is nowhere disclosed; the low/bow root pair the refrain itself uses hooks across the same seam, also undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes, and the challenge's object choice turns out to be the careful one. The four-token core מִפְּנֵי֙ פַּ֣חַד יְהוָ֔ה וּמֵהֲדַ֖ר stands at oshb:Isa.2.10 tokens 5-8, inside this row's span, and returns at oshb:Isa.2.19 tokens 6-9 and oshb:Isa.2.21 tokens 6-9 (sweep: 3 verses). Tier correction upward: on that four-token object the three sites collate at ACCENT_STRIPPED tier, one grade above the skeleton label the challenge gave them. The object had to stop where it does - a five-token run carrying the majesty noun collates NONE, because oshb:Isa.2.10 reads the defective גְּאֹנֽוֹ against the plene גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ at the later two sites - and the two later sites share an eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ that is BYTE-identical between them (sweep: 2 verses, byte). The humbling-root chain also verifies: the low/bow root stands at 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton) and in this chapter at oshb:Isa.2.9, oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.12 and oshb:Isa.2.17 - so it runs from inside this span straight across the closing seam. Why this is upheld rather than merely noted: the row's own strongest_rejected_alternative NAMES the whole-complex rival ('reading 2:5-22 as one unbroken oracle') and disposes it on the refrain digit alone. Byte-true material supporting a rival the row itself names is owed disclosure in that rival's disposal, and the motif running 2:10 to 2:19/2:21 is never engaged. Calibrating force, which is why low is right: the two recurrence sites lie beyond an intervening unit, so this is not adjacent-seam cohesion and it does not bear on the 2:11|2:12 seam directly; its force is on the complex-level rival only. What holds, independently confirmed: the onset בֵּ֖ית יַעֲקֹ֑ב לְכ֥וּ וְנֵלְכָ֖ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.5 (byte tier; the verse is 6 tokens, a vocative followed by an imperative); the closing clause וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא at oshb:Isa.2.11 tokens 8-12 collates BYTE against oshb:Isa.2.17 and וְנִשְׂגַּ֧ב יְהוָ֛ה לְבַדּ֖וֹ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַהֽוּא at oshb:Isa.2.17 tokens 7-11 collates BYTE back against oshb:Isa.2.11 - the row's two-verse digit is exact in both directions; and the row's refusal of byte-identity for the loftiness clause is correct, since שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים differs from its counterpart at oshb:Isa.2.17 in order and in the article. The SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.2.11 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span; the PE at oshb:Isa.2.4 on the opening seam is correctly typed. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2. One further engagement gap, folded into the remedy rather than counted separately: the addressee question the row honestly holds open at oshb:Isa.2.6 rests in the bytes on נָטַ֗שְׁתָּה עַמְּךָ֙ (tokens 2-3, a 2ms perfect with a 2ms suffix), and no pointed form is spliced for it anywhere in the row.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-010 device_notes, plus one clause in strongest_rejected_alternative. Change: (1) add the cross-seam disclosure naming the flight-from-terror motif with its object stated at four tokens and its tier given as accent_stripped across oshb:Isa.2.10, oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 3 verses), noting that the later two share a byte-identical eight-token run and that the earlier site's majesty noun is defective, and add the low/bow root chain (sweep: 10 verses book-wide; oshb:Isa.2.9, oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.12, oshb:Isa.2.17); (2) in the rejected alternative, dispose the whole-complex rival against that motif as well as the refrain digit; (3) splice the pointed 2ms forms behind the held addressee question. Tests the cure must pass: any tier shipped for the flight motif must reproduce under a collate of the four-token run - a run extended to include the majesty noun collates none, which is the test that fixes the object; and the disclosure must state that the recurrence sites lie beyond the intervening unit, so it is not written as adjacent-seam evidence. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: One lens: the row treats 2:12 as a fresh unit onset without disclosing that it is grammatically continuative and lexically bonded to the refrain it treats as the prior unit's clean close. The other: the rejected alternative's load-bearing form label - an asyndetic catalogue - is contradicted by the pointed bytes, which show a waw-coordinated series.
rulings.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT defects, not one defect seen twice: the first is an undisclosed cross-seam cohesion signal at the row's OPENING, the second a false form-class label inside the rejected alternative's INTERNAL-SPLIT argument. Neither subsumes the other; they sit in different fields and fail different tests. Form label, upheld and stronger than charged. Every member of the catalogue opens with the same conjunction-plus-preposition token: וְעַל֙ at oshb:Isa.2.13 token 1 and וְעַ֖ל at its token 7, and the same token at oshb:Isa.2.14 tokens 1 and 5, oshb:Isa.2.15 tokens 1 and 5, and oshb:Isa.2.16 tokens 1 and 5 - eight coordinated members, and the governing verse coordinates its own second phrase the same way (עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם at oshb:Isa.2.12 tokens 5-8 without the conjunction, וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at tokens 9-12 with it). The series is polysyndetic, the exact opposite of the label, and the label is shipped TWICE - in strongest_rejected_alternative and again in device_notes. Form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits, so this is a defect even though the conclusion it supports (enumeration inside the governing oracle) survives correction. The accompanying charge that the row calls the quantifier a preposition is right but slight: the preposition is the head and the quantifier is its object, so the two-word phrase is not simply a preposition - a wording repair inside the same edit, not a third defect. Cross-seam cohesion, upheld. oshb:Isa.2.12 opens with כִּ֣י, the same particle that opens oshb:Isa.2.6 as כִּ֣י inside the preceding row's own span, and both witnesses render it subordinating there. The humbling/lofty root chain then runs unbroken across the seam: וַיִּשַּׁ֥ח אָדָ֖ם וַיִּשְׁפַּל אִ֑ישׁ at oshb:Isa.2.9 tokens 1-4, שָׁפֵ֔ל וְשַׁ֖ח ר֣וּם אֲנָשִׁ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.11 tokens 4-7, עַ֥ל כָּל גֵּאֶ֖ה וָרָ֑ם and וְעַ֖ל כָּל נִשָּׂ֥א וְשָׁפֵֽל at oshb:Isa.2.12, הָרָמִ֖ים וְהַנִּשָּׂאִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.13 tokens 5-6 and הָרָמִ֑ים / הַנִּשָּׂאֽוֹת at oshb:Isa.2.14, closing again at oshb:Isa.2.17. Independently swept, the low/bow root alone stands at 10 verses book-wide and at exactly those four sites in this chapter (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton). That is adjacent-verse cohesion straddling this row's own opening seam, undisclosed, and it leaves the strongest rival - one sustained pride-and-humbling poem with the refrain as internal punctuation - unstated. Recorded but NOT counted as a defect: the flight-from-terror motif brackets this row with no member inside its span. A device lying wholly on both sides of a row argues at complex level only; it cannot argue continuity ACROSS either of this row's own seams, so it is a chapter-level note, not a cross-seam disclosure this row owes. What holds: the opening run is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.2.12 at byte tier; the closing refrain clause is verse-final and byte-identical to the earlier site (sweep: 2 verses, byte); no parashah mark falls inside 2:12-2:17 and the SAMEKH cited at the opening seam is correctly typed - mark handling is complete and honest. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2. Severity: the two items differ in weight - the cohesion gap touches the onset warrant, the form label is contained to a rival's internal reasoning - and the combined grade is set by the heavier.
rulings.remedy: Two fields, two independent edits. (1) strongest_rejected_alternative and device_notes: replace the asyndetic label with the waw-coordinated (polysyndetic) description, and re-cut the quantifier wording so the preposition is named as head and the quantifier as its object; the internal-split rejection itself stands, since a coordinated series still hangs on the governing temporal clause. (2) device_notes: add the cross-seam disclosure at the opening seam - the subordinating particle shared with oshb:Isa.2.6, and the humbling/lofty root chain running oshb:Isa.2.9, oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.12, oshb:Isa.2.13-14, oshb:Isa.2.17 (sweep: 10 verses book-wide, skeleton) - and state the sustained-poem rival it raises. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected form label must survive a token read of oshb:Isa.2.13 through oshb:Isa.2.16 showing the conjunction on every member - the test that killed the original; and the cohesion disclosure must be tier-labelled per site, since the chain is a root-level link, not a byte recurrence. No boundary change is proposed; adopting the sustained-poem rival would be a boss decision, never author work.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated ground for this row's opening seam - a fresh topical turn to the idols at 2:18 - is contested by the bytes, since the idol lexeme is already in the preceding row at 2:8 and the flight-from-terror formula of 2:10 returns inside this row at 2:19 and 2:21.
rulings.grounds: The digits verify and one of the two grounds does not survive re-derivation. Idol half, refuted on its own bytes. The lexeme stands at 8 verses book-wide and in this chapter at oshb:Isa.2.8, oshb:Isa.2.18 and oshb:Isa.2.20 (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton) - digits exact. But the challenge places the first site 'inside the preceding row', and it is not: אֱלִילִ֑ים at oshb:Isa.2.8 lies inside the 2:5-2:11 span, two rows upstream. The row immediately preceding this one is 2:12-2:17, and its bytes carry NO idol lexeme at any of its six verses. The row's own wording is scoped to exactly that adjacent unit - a fresh topical turn 'after the stanza-closing refrain of verse 17' - and against the adjacent unit the turn genuinely is fresh. The resumption the challenge sees is real but operates at complex level, and the row already concedes complex-level continuity in device_notes by disclosing the temporal tag at oshb:Isa.2.20 (בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙). This ground does not stand. Flight half, upheld, and this is the row's real defect. Two members of the motif sit INSIDE this span - מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר at oshb:Isa.2.19 tokens 6-9 and the same four-token core at oshb:Isa.2.21 tokens 6-9 - while a third sits beyond the row's opening seam at oshb:Isa.2.10 (accent_stripped tier across the three on that object; the run collates none once the majesty noun is included, since the earlier site is defective). A device with a member inside the span and a member across the seam is adjacent-seam cohesion in the strict sense, and it is undisclosed. Second and separate: the eight-token run מִפְּנֵ֞י פַּ֤חַד יְהוָה֙ וּמֵהֲדַ֣ר גְּאוֹנ֔וֹ בְּקוּמ֖וֹ לַעֲרֹ֥ץ הָאָֽרֶץ is BYTE-identical between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte), an in-span repetition of a strength the row never mentions while disclosing only the weaker temporal tag at its third verse. Corrected finding and severity: one stated ground is sound as scoped, the other is replaced by a genuine two-part disclosure gap that does not touch the bounds - so the grade drops from the charged level. What holds: the quoted opening run וְהָאֱלִילִ֖ים כָּלִ֥יל יַחֲלֹֽף is the entire verse at byte tier (oshb:Isa.2.18 is 3 tokens); the PE at oshb:Isa.2.22 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span; and the rejected alternative's negative claim is exact - the stanza-closing clause occurs at exactly 2 verses book-wide (oshb:Isa.2.11, oshb:Isa.2.17, byte tier) and at neither end of this row. The second idol site inside the span, אֱלִילֵ֣י at oshb:Isa.2.20 token 6, confirms the subject is genuinely this row's own. Identity numbering; no ketiv/qere note in chapter 2.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-012 device_notes. Change: add two tier-labelled disclosures - the flight-from-terror motif straddling the opening seam (four-token object, accent_stripped tier across oshb:Isa.2.10, oshb:Isa.2.19, oshb:Isa.2.21; sweep: 3 verses), and the byte-identical eight-token repetition between oshb:Isa.2.19 and oshb:Isa.2.21 (sweep: 2 verses, byte). Leave the boundary_rationale's fresh-turn wording standing: it is scoped to the adjacent refrain-closed unit and the bytes support it there. If the complex-level idol resumption is added at all, it must be written as complex-level and must name where the first site actually lies. Tests the cure must pass: the flight disclosure must reproduce its tier on the four-token object; and any statement about the idol lexeme must name the row that actually contains oshb:Isa.2.8 - the locus error that made the original ground look decisive. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: The bounds hold, but the row's own stated cut criterion is met at an undisclosed in-span site - the verse-initial imperative at 3:10 - and its lexeme distinction is argued with no pointed form at all.
rulings.grounds: Both halves re-derive exactly. The in-span rival: oshb:Isa.3.10 is 8 tokens opening אִמְר֥וּ (token 1, byte tier), a 2mp imperative. Independently swept, that pointed form reaches accent_stripped tier at exactly 5 verses book-wide (sweep: 5 verses - oshb:Isa.3.10, oshb:Isa.35.4, oshb:Isa.36.4, oshb:Isa.48.20, oshb:Isa.62.11), every one an imperative address. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative rules out an earlier cut precisely on the ground that the candidate verse carries 'no fresh imperative, vocative, or divine-speech formula of its own'. By the row's OWN criterion the verse-initial imperative two verses later is a live in-span rival, and it is neither disclosed nor disposed. That is an incomplete rival disposal on a criterion the row itself set. The engagement gap: device_notes states the interjection distinction entirely in transliteration, with no pointed splice for either lexeme, in a book where that pair is a named blending hazard. The distinction the row draws is CORRECT - byte-verified, א֣וֹי stands at oshb:Isa.3.9 token 10 and א֖וֹי at oshb:Isa.3.11 token 1, and independently swept the interjection is a 4-verse token object (oshb:Isa.3.9, oshb:Isa.3.11, oshb:Isa.6.5, oshb:Isa.24.16) while a bare three-letter substring sweep returns 8 verses, the extra 4 being contained-consonant hits inside unrelated words at oshb:Isa.1.24, oshb:Isa.26.9, oshb:Isa.35.8 and oshb:Isa.63.10; the woe-onset lexeme it is distinguished from stands at 22 verses (sweep: 22 verses, skeleton). So the defect is engagement, not accuracy: a boundary-relevant Hebrew claim carrying the weight of a not-cut decision ships with no pointed splice. Severity low is right: the default-larger-unit rule absorbs the 3:10 rival and the span is not defeated. What holds: כִּי֩ הִנֵּ֨ה הָאָד֜וֹן יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.1 (byte tier); the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.12 is correctly typed and the only parashah mark inside 3:1-3:12; the PE cited at the opening seam is correctly typed; and neither of the chapter's two ketiv/qere verses falls inside this span, so nothing is owed there. Identity numbering.
rulings.remedy: Two fields. (1) P01-013 strongest_rejected_alternative or device_notes: disclose the verse-initial imperative at oshb:Isa.3.10 as an in-span rival raised by the row's own criterion, and dispose it explicitly - the default-larger-unit rule is the available disposal, but it must be stated rather than left silent. (2) P01-013 device_notes: splice both pointed interjection forms from source and label the swept objects and digits alongside the transliteration (the interjection at 4 verses token-exact; the woe-onset lexeme at 22 verses; the contained-consonant hazard named). Tests the cure must pass: the disposal must apply the row's own stated criterion to oshb:Isa.3.10 rather than restating the criterion - silence under one's own test is what killed the original; and any interjection digit shipped must distinguish the token-exact object from the substring sweep, since the substring returns twice the count. No boundary change is proposed.

rulings.challenge_claim: One lens: the row's disclosed rival addresses a unit_type labeling choice rather than a genuine competing boundary, leaving its actual strongest segmentation rival unstated. The other: this row survives every check applied to it, but its superlative carries no digit and is scoped to a work partition rather than to the text.
rulings.grounds: Both items are real and they are DISTINCT: different fields, different failure classes, and neither subsumes the other. Missing segmentation rival, upheld and the weightier of the two. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative argues trial_speech against judgment_oracle - an operative-category choice - and names no competing span at all. The identical disclosure already stands in device_notes as the mandated deviation note, so the field is duplicated onto a classification argument and the row ships with NO tested boundary rival: whether these three verses merge back into the leadership-collapse unit that precedes them, or run on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16, is never weighed. A mandated disclosure field carrying no instance of what it exists to disclose is a genuine defect, not a stylistic one. Undigited partition-scoped superlative, upheld. The boundary_rationale calls this the clearest contend-and-judge pairing 'in this part' - a superlative with no digit-bearing sweep naming object and unit, scoped to a workflow partition rather than to a verse range or to the book, and workflow references do not belong in row prose. Re-derived independently, the bytes license a stronger and fully checkable replacement: לָרִ֖יב at oshb:Isa.3.13 token 2 stands at 3 verses token-exact (sweep: 3 verses, skeleton - oshb:Isa.3.13, oshb:Isa.34.8, oshb:Isa.58.4) and לָדִ֥ין at token 5 at exactly 1 (sweep: 1 verse, skeleton), so the pairing cannot recur anywhere else in the book - a book-scoped digit-bearing claim replacing a partition-scoped undigited one. Cross-row note: this partition-reference class recurs at P01-016, which brackets images over 'the part's own' range twice. It is a register sweep across the cluster, not two spot fixes. What holds, and it is most of the row: נִצָּ֥ב לָרִ֖יב יְהוָ֑ה וְעֹמֵ֖ד לָדִ֥ין עַמִּֽים is verse-initial and exhausts oshb:Isa.3.13 at byte tier (6 tokens); the closing signature נְאֻם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִ֖ה צְבָאֽוֹת is verse-final at oshb:Isa.3.15 tokens 9-12 at byte tier with the exact title stack quoted rather than blended with the differently stacked signature earlier in the book; the ketiv/qere disclosure is exact and unusually careful - oshb:Isa.3.15 carries one note whose unpointed ketiv מלכם stands at token 1 with its pointed qere, eight tokens before the quoted signature, so the quoted run is genuinely unaffected exactly as the row says; the SAMEKH at oshb:Isa.3.15 is correctly typed and the only mark in the span, and the SAMEKH at the opening seam is correctly typed too. Identity numbering. Severity is set by the heavier item: an untested mandated rival outweighs a prose-and-digit repair.
rulings.remedy: Two fields, one edit each. (1) P01-014 strongest_rejected_alternative: replace the classification argument with an actual segmentation rival and dispose it on bytes - the two live candidates are merging back into the preceding leadership-collapse unit and running on to the narrative onset at oshb:Isa.3.16 - and leave the operative-category deviation disclosure where it already correctly lives, in device_notes. (2) P01-014 boundary_rationale: drop the workflow-partition scope and re-cut the superlative to a book-scoped digit-bearing claim (contend infinitive 3 verses, judge infinitive 1 verse, the pairing unique to this verse). Tests the cure must pass: the rewritten rival must name a competing SPAN and be disposed on the row's own bytes - a field that names no span fails the same test again; the re-cut superlative must carry a digit whose object is named and must contain no workflow reference; and the two disclosures must not restate one another, since duplication is what emptied the field. No boundary change is proposed - naming a rival is not adopting it.

rulings.challenge_claim: The row's own grammatical label for the Isa.3.18-23 catalogue is imprecise - that verse opens with a single finite verb governing an accumulating list of accusative objects, not a construct/genitive chain as the row's prose labels it - though the underlying single-unit conclusion is sound.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from bytes and the label is a category error. oshb:Isa.3.18 is 9 tokens: בַּיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא at tokens 1-2 (the temporal formula), יָסִ֣יר at token 3 - a single finite verb - with its subject אֲדֹנָ֗י at token 4, the direct-object marker אֵ֣ת at token 5, and then the objects beginning תִּפְאֶ֧רֶת הָעֲכָסִ֛ים וְהַשְּׁבִיסִ֖ים וְהַשַּׂהֲרֹנִֽים. The row's strongest_rejected_alternative calls the catalogue 'grammatically one long construct chain governed by' the opening clause. A construct chain is a genitive nominal sequence; what governs here is a finite verb reaching its objects through the object marker. Individual items in the list are themselves construct phrases, which is the likely source of the slip, but the catalogue as a whole is an accusative object series, not one chain. Form-class labels are byte-checkable claims held to the same discipline as digits, so the label is a defect on its own terms. Severity low is right and the challenge says so itself: the conclusion the label supports - enumeration inside one governed clause rather than an independent list-register unit - is correct, and the owner-ruled list-register finding independently reaches the same result for this very catalogue. Correcting the label strengthens the argument rather than unsettling it, since a single finite verb reaching across six verses is a tighter grammatical bond than a construct chain would be. What holds, checked in full because the other lens supported this row: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֗ה is verse-initial at oshb:Isa.3.16 (byte tier) and the row's role-split is right - this is the narrative onset class, not the postpositive signature class closing the preceding row. The ketiv/qere disclosure is exact: oshb:Isa.3.16 carries one note staged as a doubled token pair mid-verse, the unpointed ketiv נטוות at token 9 with its pointed qere נְטוּי֣וֹת at token 10, well after the quoted onset, so the row's statement that the onset is unaffected is true. Mark symmetry is complete and correctly typed across the whole span - a SAMEKH inside the span at oshb:Isa.3.17, overridden with a stated reason, a SAMEKH at the closing verse oshb:Isa.4.1, and a SAMEKH at the opening seam - with no undisclosed parashah mark anywhere in the range. The contested chapter-crossing is byte-supportable and holds: oshb:Isa.4.1 opens וְהֶחֱזִיקוּ֩, a waw-prefixed perfect continuing the sequence begun at וְאָנ֥וּ וְאָבְל֖וּ (oshb:Isa.3.26 tokens 1-2), with no fresh frame, vocative or imperative at that verse. Identity numbering. One reservation the other lens raised and I confirm, folded into the remedy: the row argues that crossing from the English rendering alone and never splices the waw-prefixed form, so its riskiest decision rests on translation-visible grounds.
rulings.remedy: Field: P01-015 strongest_rejected_alternative (and any echo of the label in device_notes). Change: replace 'one long construct chain' with the byte-true description - a single finite verb at oshb:Isa.3.18 token 3 governing, through the object marker at token 5, an accumulating series of accusative objects across the catalogue - keeping the conclusion, which the corrected grammar supports more strongly. While in the row, splice the waw-prefixed perfect at oshb:Isa.4.1 and the sequence it continues at oshb:Isa.3.26 so the chapter-crossing rests on the bytes rather than on the rendering. Tests the cure must pass: the corrected label must survive a token read of oshb:Isa.3.18 showing a finite verb plus object marker rather than a genitive sequence - the test that killed the original; and the crossing argument must cite a pointed form, since a translation-only warrant is what left the row's riskiest decision unengaged. No boundary change is proposed; the span is unaffected.

rulings.challenge_claim: One lens: the row's remnant-family signal tag blends two lexically distinct roots at Isa.4.3 as if they were one family. The other: the same blend, plus an opening-seam temporal formula that straddles the seam undisclosed, plus an echo claim that mis-states the attached form and the matching tier while bracketing a work partition rather than a unit of text.
rulings.grounds: Convergence first: the remnant item is the SAME defect independently reached by both lenses; the temporal-formula and echo items are DISTINCT additions only one lens reached. All three verify. Remnant blend (shared), upheld. oshb:Isa.4.3 carries הַנִּשְׁאָ֣ר at token 2 and וְהַנּוֹתָר֙ at token 4, both byte tier, and they are from two different roots. The row quotes them together as one 'remnant clause' and tags the pair under a single reactivating-verb signal key. The book's remnant family is a four-object set on ONE root, and the second word here is not a member of it: its own root is what opens oshb:Isa.1.8 as וְנוֹתְרָ֥ה, standing at 4 verses book-wide by substring and at exactly 1 verse as this token-exact form (sweep: 1 verse). A blended sweep under one semantic-class key is what the count discipline forbids, and it is the more striking because the row extends careful root-and-tier attention to the shelter echo in the very same field.
